gushehClassifier.caption: Compare Modally Specific gūshehs (tied to a distinct secondary maqām) with Modally Non-Specific gūshehs like Kereshmeh, whose signature rhythmic-melodic contour adapts to different modes.

items.title: Delkash (in Māhūr)
items.description: Introduces a distinct secondary maqām in the upper register of Māhūr with its own characteristic accidental (A-koron) and focal pitch.

items.title: Kereshmeh (adapted to Māhūr)
items.description: Kereshmeh has no fixed maqām of its own; its signature rhythmic-melodic pattern here takes the pitches of Māhūr (C–D–E–F).

items.title: Kereshmeh (same pattern in Shūr)
items.description: The exact same Kereshmeh rhythmic-melodic contour now mapped onto the Shūr dāng (D–E-koron–F–G), demonstrating modal portability.

gushehEtymology.caption: Filter gūsheh names by their etymological origin to see how geography, tribes, emotions, historical figures, and poetry shaped the Radif's vocabulary.

categories.label: Cities & Regions
categories.note: Named after historical cities and regions across Greater Iran and the broader Islamic world.

categories.label: Tribes & Peoples
categories.note: Reflecting regional and tribal musical idioms absorbed into the classical repertoire.

categories.label: Emotional States
categories.note: Directly describing the expressive affect or mood evoked by the gūsheh.

categories.label: Historical Figures
categories.note: Preserving the names of historical patrons, musicians, or rulers.

categories.label: Poetic Forms
categories.note: Named after classical Persian poetic genres and meters closely paired with those melodies.

categories.label: Uncertain Origin
categories.note: Traditional names whose original historical derivation is no longer definitively known.

radifTree.caption: Inspect each layer of the Tree of Persian Classical Music—from ancient roots and the Radif trunk up to live improvisation.

layers.label: Leaves & Fruit
layers.detail: Live performances, taṣnīfs, pīsh-darāmads, and improvisations—all nourished by the modal sap flowing from the Radif.

layers.label: Twigs
layers.detail: Individual modal and rhythmic models built from dāngs, key scale degrees (ش، خ، ی، م، آ), and sarmashqs, unified via Darāmad and Forūd.

layers.label: 5 Sub-Branches
layers.detail: Subsidiary systems: Abū'aṭā, Bayāt-e Tork, Afshārī, and Dashtī (from Shūr), plus Bayāt-e Eṣfahān (from Homāyūn).

layers.label: 7 Main Branches
layers.detail: Shūr, Navā, Segāh, Chahārgāh, Homāyūn, Māhūr, and Rāst-Panjgāh—each a multi-modal cycle anchored by its mother maqām.

layers.label: Trunk
layers.detail: Codified repertoire of melodic models: Mirzā Abdollāh & Āqā Ḥoseynqolī (instrumental), Davāmī & Karīmī (vocal), and Ma'rūfī's 1963 compilation.

layers.label: Roots
layers.detail: Centuries of collective aesthetic evolution, modal theory, and oral transmission forming the historical foundation.
